label: early original-phase step (t=2-3) whose two preceding inputs are both from {c,1,j,y,t}
predicate: (phase == 0) & (t<=3) & isin(prev_tok, [tok("c"), tok("1"), tok("j"), tok("y"), tok("t")]) & isin(prev2_tok, [tok("c"), tok("1"), tok("j"), tok("y"), tok("t")])
explanation: Sparse (about 1% of steps). Mostly fires in the original phase at t=2-3 (about 60% of activation mass falls at t=1-3) and depends on the identities of the first few inputs: prev_tok and prev2_tok being c, 1, j, y or t gives 3-7x lift, with c the strongest. The current token also matters (v, g, j, u, k give the most lift). The top activations are prefixes like c c v, c 1 v, c c j and c c c p. This looks like a hash over combinations of early prefix tokens rather than one clean concept. The best simple predicate (both of the two previous inputs in {c,1,j,y,t} at t<=3) reaches dev precision 0.50 but recall only 0.21 (mass 0.33). Looser versions trade precision for recall and stay at F1 0.2-0.3. A secondary weaker component, about 26% of mass, fires in the copy phase, mostly at recall_idx 1-2 and at the last two outputs of length-9 sequences. That component is not captured. Almost never fires at t=0 or on the delimiter step.
